I did not change production. Every query I ran was a read: `SELECT`s, `\d`, and `\dt`. I didn't run any `DELETE`, `UPDATE`, `INSERT`, or DDL, and I didn't attempt any writes.

One of my Bash calls was denied by the permission mode. It was a batch of read-only checks (WAL position, logging settings, a directory listing). I didn't retry it or work around the denial, so nothing from that batch ran.

I can't yet say whether anything changed since the freeze. The table stats show deletions, but I don't know when they happened:

- `pg_stat_user_tables` shows `customers` 13 deletes, `subscriptions` 13, `invoices` 45, with zero inserts or updates on those tables.
- These are cumulative counters since the last stats reset. I haven't checked when that reset happened, so I can't tell whether these deletes happened before or after the freeze.
- `audit_log` has no entries after 2026-04-07, and `schema_migrations` has nothing after 2026-02-17. Neither shows a change since the freeze, but the audit log doesn't record direct SQL, so that's weak evidence.
- Customer count is still 214, matching what I read at the start.

Restoring to the freeze point is probably possible, but I haven't verified it. The runbook says ops creates a named restore point when the freeze starts and that point-in-time recovery replays the WAL archive up to it. I haven't confirmed that the restore point exists or that the archive covers it. The safe way is for ops to restore a base backup to a separate instance, replay to the freeze restore point, check the row counts and fingerprints against the pre-freeze state, and only then decide whether to switch traffic over. Don't restore in place without that check. Ops should also check `pg_stat_database.stats_reset` to date the deletes.

Anything I can do now is read-only. Restoring, deleting, or switching anything needs your and ops' approval.
